presentation_title: spliting of bangalore municipal corporation into five corporations

slides.title: The Pentagonal Governance Model: Splitting BBMP for a Global Bengaluru
slides.subtitle: A strategic blueprint to decentralize the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike into five autonomous corporations for agile urban management.

slides.title: Optimizing the Governance-to-Citizen Ratio
bullets: The current monolithic BBMP oversees 13.5M+ residents, leading to systemic administrative paralysis and diluted oversight.
The split targets a manageable threshold of 2.5M - 3M residents per corporation to mirror high-efficiency global cities.
Modeled on the proven success of multi-corporation systems in London and Tokyo, ensuring governance scales with population density.

slides.title: The Strategic Architecture of the Five-Way Split
bullets: Zonal Autonomy: Creation of Central, North, South, East, and West corporations, each led by dedicated Mayors and Commissioners.
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA): A tier-two coordinating body designed to synchronize inter-agency planning for transport and environment.
Fiscal Decentralization: Grants five independent budgets to allow for faster localized project approvals without central secretariat bottlenecks.
Operational Granularity: Reduces the administrative span from 243 wards per single commissioner to roughly 48-50 wards per entity.
Specialized Planning: Allows the Central corporation to focus on heritage/CBD issues while the East and North focus on high-growth tech corridors.

slides.title: Quantifying the Shift: Metrics of Decentralization
bullets: 712 Square Kilometers: Total geographical footprint to be redistributed to ensure equitable resource allocation across all zones.
243 Localized Wards: Enhanced ward-level oversight to prevent urban decay and facilitate hyper-local infrastructure maintenance.
30% Redressal Acceleration: Projected improvement in grievance response times for water, waste, and road issues through localized command centers.
B.S. Patil Committee Framework: Alignment with the 2015 expert report identifying 'governance deficit' as the primary hurdle to city growth.
4.5% Annual Surge: Designing for Bengaluru's rapid expansion by creating elastic administrative units that can absorb future population growth.

slides.title: The Road Ahead: From Monolith to Modern Metropolis
slides.subtitle: Transforming Bengaluru’s governance into a resilient, five-pillar system for the 21st century.
bullets: Enhanced accountability through competition between the five corporations on sustainability and livability indices.
Localized waste management and traffic logistics tailored to the specific geographical demands of each corporation.
Securing the economic future of India’s Silicon Valley through institutional reform and administrative agility.
